text:
maria_gomez: FYI customer reported spikes of 502 + auth failures after last night's canary. They say tail latency jumped and some requests got 401s even though their token is valid.
alex_kim: ugh, any request ids?
daniel_cho: they provided a set: req_8b3f2a4c, req_8b3f2b10, req_8b3f2c91 — all from the same 10-min window.
maria_gomez: pasted one full example from customer: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-XXXX
X-Request-ID: req_8b3f2a4c
Content-Type: application/json
{ "model": "beta-large-v2-canary", "input": "Summarize this..." }
```

sre-oncall: :eyes: I see an internal trace for req_8b3f2a4c, shows upstream 502 at model-proxy and then a fallback to stable, but there are also auth:error entries right before. Attaching a short log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-16T22:11:03Z] req=req_8b3f2a4c auth=ok token_ttl=0s WARN token-expired, refresh-failed
[2026-03-16T22:11:03Z] req=req_8b3f2a4c proxy=beta-large-v2-canary upstream=502 fallback=redwood-base-v1 latency_ms=1180
[2026-03-16T22:11:03Z] req=req_8b3f2a4c proxy=redwood-base-v1 result=200 latency_ms=240
```

alex_kim: token_ttl=0s is interesting — either the customer token actually expired or our auth cache TTL eviction is broken. Can customer repro with a curl that includes a fresh token?
maria_gomez: customer says curl worked sometimes and failed sometimes, reliable in 5/10 attempts. Asked them to run a curl loop but they want clear repro steps.

daniel_cho: ok, standard repro instructions to request:
1) capture request id header and timestamp when it fails
2) run a tight curl loop with an explicit X-Request-ID and model param to reproduce the path
3) call our debug-bundle endpoint with those request ids and trace ids

Paste suggested curl we can give them:
```
for i in {1..20}; do
  RID="manual-$(date +%s)-$i"
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <FRESH_TOKEN>" \
    -H "X-Request-ID: $RID" \
    -H "X-Client-Name: acme-app" \
    -d '{"model":"beta-large-v2-canary","input":"short ping"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  sleep 0.3
done
```

support-bot: reminder: customers should never post real keys in Slack. Ask them to redact. :lock:

alex_kim: also ask them to include the raw response body when they get 401/502, and the exact server time — we need to correlate with auth cache TTL evictions.
maria_gomez: sending repro steps now. I also asked for one full debug bundle: `POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug/bundles` JSON body {"request_id":"req_8b3f2a4c"} (they need to be org admin or give us a signed upload)

sre-oncall: while we wait, please do a quick check: eng-releases, any canary rollout changes last night touching auth cache or token refresh?

eng-releases: we rolled beta-large-v2-canary at 21:45 UTC. No intended auth changes, but we did change the routing policy to prefer canary nodes in us-east-1 which changed cache affinity.

daniel_cho: that could explain TTL=0 if requests hit a newly spun canary pod with empty auth cache. Two lines of attack: pin this customer->stable model to avoid fallback churn, and collect pod logs & auth cache stats from canary nodes.

eng-releases: I can pin the customer by adding a routing override for their org id to redwood-base-v1 for 1 hour. Need customer org id.
maria_gomez: org id is org_991122. Doing it now.

support-bot: deploy-hook: routing override applied -> org_991122 -> redwood-base-v1 (expires in 60m).

alex_kim: good. Also provide the customer an explicit header they can use to force stable for testing: `-H "X-Model-Pin: stable"` or `{"model_version":"redwood-base-v1"}` in payload.
maria_gomez: customer tried `model_version` but didn't know about X-Model-Pin. Sending both.

sre-oncall: after pinning, monitor for 10-15m. If errors drop to near-zero for that org, we have strong signal it was routing/cache related. Meanwhile eng-releases, please collect auth cache metrics from canary node pool and dump KV keys evicted around 21:40-22:15 UTC.

eng-releases: will pull: nodes: canary-us-east-1-{a,b,c}. I'll attach logs to the thread once I have them.

maria_gomez: customer ran the curl loop with X-Model-Pin: stable and reported 0 failures in 50 runs. With no pin they still see ~40% failures. They uploaded a debug bundle id dbg_20260316_2212 (gave us a signed link).

daniel_cho: perfect repro. That triangulates to the canary affinity issue. Next steps:
- eng to extract auth cache snapshot and compare TTLs
- eng to run a small reconfigure to warm cache on canary nodes (or revert routing affinity)
- product/ops to schedule a controlled rollback if warming is insufficient

eng-releases: extracted the cache snapshot, saw many tokens with ttl=0 at canary-start time. Looks like a race on cache population when pods join the pool. We can push a hotfix to pre-warm or change routing to prefer nodes with warmed caches.

sre-oncall: recommend we keep the override pin for org_991122 until the hotfix is live and validated. :thumbsup:

maria_gomez: customer confirmed they can proceed with their deployment if we keep pin set. They asked for an ETA on fix.

eng-releases: tentative hotfix deploy in ~2 hours, with a canary of the hotfix to a single node then gradual rollout. We'll post updates.

support-bot: note: saved artifacts -> debug_bundle:dbg_20260316_2212, logs: canary-us-east-1-a.{link}

alex_kim: thanks everyone. Follow-up items: tag this thread with incident id INC-2026-0316-auth-cache, and once hotfix is validated, we can remove the routing override and confirm no regression with 100-run curl smoke tests.
maria_gomez: tagging and closing for now, will reopen if customer sees new failures. :white_check_mark:
